evidence_quotes: 150 earthquakes were recorded over the 30-day period, averaging 5 events per day
the busiest days falling on February 3 and February 14 (9 events each)
Magnitudes ranged from M4.0 to M6.2, with an average of M4.62
Tobelo, Indonesia led all regions with 19 events, followed by Mohr, Iran (15), Nikolski, Alaska (13), Hachinohe, Japan (11), and Lata, Solomon Islands (10)
events near Tual, Indonesia (depth 2.0 km), Hachinohe, Japan (4.1 km), and off Honshu, Japan (2.7 km)
No tsunami warnings were triggered across any of the 30 sample events logged
patterns that can sometimes precede larger events or indicate ongoing fault stress accumulation
criticisms: The report states 'No tsunami warnings were triggered across any of the 30 sample events logged' — the digest provides exactly 30 sample_events, all with tsunami=false, so this is technically accurate for the sample, but the report implies this covers all 150 events, which is not verifiable from the digest. This is a minor overreach.
The report says 'averaging 5 events per day' — 150 events over 30 days equals exactly 5.0 per day, which is correct and traceable.

The Hachinohe, Japan shallow event cited (depth 4.1 km) corresponds to the event at '80 km E of Hachinohe, Japan' in the digest — the report drops the directional qualifier, slightly misrepresenting the place name, though Hachinohe does appear in the digest.
The 'off Honshu, Japan' event at depth 2.7 km is correctly traceable to the sample event 'Off coast of Honshu, Japan' at depth 2.7 km — this checks out.
The final bullet uses cautious hedging ('can sometimes precede') which is acceptable monitoring framing, not a specific prediction — this passes the no_unsupported_predictions check.
The Mohr, Iran shallow events referenced are supported by sample events showing depths of 8.5 km and 1.9 km — the characterization of 'multiple shallow strikes' is defensible.
